title: Brent Interview — The 2025 Numbers (quiz)
description: Broadview's 2025 Annual Report figures (all verified 21 Aug 2026): group, regions, Energy, Westag, cash, debt, FX, sustainability, financing, and the bridges between them. Practice + multiple-choice quiz with 5–6 distractors per card.

cards.front: Group revenue and recurring EBITDA, 2025 vs 2024?
cards.back: Revenue €1,238.2m vs €1,259.8m (−1.7%; −0.7% organic and currency-adjusted). Recurring EBITDA €105.7m vs €130.0m (−18.7%). Calculated recurring margin ~8.5% vs ~10.3%.
distractors: Revenue €1,238m (−8.7%); recurring EBITDA €105.7m vs €130.0m (−1.7%).
Revenue €1,360m (+1.7%); recurring EBITDA €130.0m vs €105.7m (+23%).

Revenue €1,132m (−2.7%); recurring EBITDA €105.5m vs €129.0m (−18%).
Revenue €1,238m (−1.7%); recurring EBITDA €125.0m vs €130.0m (−4%).
cards.hint: Revenue barely moved; profit fell ten times faster.

cards.front: What is the one-sentence diagnosis of 2025?
cards.back: A margin story, not a revenue story: sales −1.7% but recurring EBITDA −18.7% — operating leverage in reverse (fixed manufacturing costs over fewer units), plus higher opex, the switch to a non-US kraft-paper supplier and US import tariffs; concentrated in Europe, offset by North America.
cards.quizAnswer: Margin and operating-leverage problem, not a sales collapse; Europe weak, North America up.
distractors: A sales collapse driven by losing major customers to Wilsonart and EGGER.
A one-off hit from the Valencia flood; underlying profit was flat.
A currency story: all of the decline is euro translation of USD results.
A growth story: revenue up strongly but profit reinvested in capacity.
An Energy-cluster problem; Materials profit was stable.

cards.front: What did Broadview pay to increase its Westag stake, and to what level?
cards.back: A further 13% for €18m in 2025, taking ownership to 89.8% (from 76.8%). Westag was delisted on 1 Jul 2025 after a delisting agreement and takeover offer via Broadview Industries AG. Signals continued strategic conviction despite short-term pressure.

cards.front: Sustainability footprint — numbers and the caveat?
cards.back: Cradle-to-gate emissions 420kt CO2e (2019) → 240kt (2025), below the ~300kt target (−29% by 2026). Decomposition: −101kt from lower volumes, −97kt from reduction projects, +17kt from LCA refinements. Chemicals and fossil fuels are the main positive drivers; wood/paper biogenic carbon reduces the modelled footprint. Judge per-unit progress, not headline tonnes.
cards.quizAnswer: 420kt → 240kt CO2e, but about half the cut came from lower volumes, not projects.
distractors: 420kt → 240kt CO2e, entirely from efficiency projects and green electricity.

cards.front: Key financing facts a finance trainee should know?
cards.back: Broadview Materials €160m ABN AMRO/HSBC facility (€120m term + €40m RCF, fully drawn), maturing Mar 2027 with extension options to 2029; leverage covenant <3.5x, complied; €44.3m undrawn elsewhere. Schuldschein remnants €15.6m + €65m (Trespa), €25m due Jun 2026. Arpa: new €10m Intesa loan (2031). Formica Asia loans €14.6m due 2026. Interest paid €26.3m. Interim dividend €5.0m. Refinancing is near — cash conversion matters now.
cards.quizAnswer: €160m Materials facility matures 2027 (covenant <3.5x); shareholder loans €518m; interest €26m.
distractors: No bank debt — entirely financed by HAL shareholder loans of €700m.
€500m bond maturing 2030 with a 2.0x covenant; no shareholder loans.

cards.hint: Why is cash a board-level topic? Because 2027 is close.

cards.front: What happened at Formica Valencia, start to finish?
cards.back: Flood in Oct 2024; decision in early 2025 not to resume production; ~135 employees affected; restructuring cost €9.9m offset by €6.3m insurance; volumes fully transferred to other group factories; Spanish commercial activities consolidated into Broadview Materials Spain with a new distribution centre in Valencia; former factory sold at book value on 27 Jan 2026. The real-life precedent for any production-transfer case.
cards.quizAnswer: Flooded Oct 2024, closed 2025, volumes moved to other plants, site sold Jan 2026.
distractors: Rebuilt after the flood and reopened with new presses in 2026.
Sold as a going concern to Abet Laminati in 2025.
Closed for cost reasons in 2023, before the flood, and converted to a warehouse.
Flooded Oct 2024, still idle pending an insurance dispute.
Merged with Arpa's Bra plant; workers relocated to Italy.

cards.front: How did HAL, the owner, describe Broadview's 2025?
cards.back: HAL Annual Report (27 Mar 2026): Broadview (97.4%) revenue €1,238m, EBITDA €106m, EBITA €40m vs €58m — 'revenues decreased 1.7% due to lower materials volumes, and operating income decreased… driven by reduced volumes and the impact of U.S. tariffs, partly offset by efficiency programs'; HAL book value €686m. HAL's H1-2026 report is due 27 Aug 2026 — after the interview.

distractors: Strong volume recovery in Europe; EBITA doubled to €116m.
